title: Waiting for a Warmer Day
statement: You have the weather forecast for the next **n** days: t[1], ..., t[n]. For every day you want to know the temperature of the **first later day that is strictly warmer**. If no later day is warmer, write -1 for that day.
input:
The first line contains an integer **n**.

The second line contains n integers t[1], ..., t[n].
output: Print n integers on one line separated by spaces. The i-th number is the temperature of the first day j > i with t[j] > t[i], or -1 if there is no such day.

samples.explanation: After day 3 (temperature 3) the first warmer day is day 4 with 5. Nothing after day 2 is warmer than 7.

hints: For each day, scanning to the right until a warmer day is found can take O(n^2) in total (think of a decreasing forecast).
Process days from right to left and keep a stack of candidate temperatures. Pop everything that is not warmer than the current day: it can never be the answer for any earlier day.
editorial:
Use a monotonic stack. Go from the last day to the first. Before answering day i, pop from the stack all values ≤ t[i]; they are hidden behind day i for every earlier day. Now the top of the stack (if any) is the next warmer temperature, otherwise the answer is -1. Then push t[i]. Every value is pushed and popped at most once.

Complexity: O(n).
